approach: Give the planner the deadline it runs under, and a way to pace against it. Add `deadline_s: u64` to `PlannerInputs` (planner.rs:33) and a `pub(super) const DEADLINE_RULE` with a root-cause doc comment, following CODE_CLAIMS_RULE (planner.rs:82-90) and the producer's `time_budget_section` (briefs.rs:758-776). `planner_brief` renders the rule in its own `## Deadline` section after the revision block and before `## Report` (planner.rs:156), so first-round and revision briefs both carry it. The rule states the deadline in seconds and says a planner stopped at the deadline sends no plan. Answering finding 1, it also says the planner has no clock: its grant is Read, Grep and Glob with an empty command map (planning.rs:656-663), so the stop point is a reading order it can count tool calls against, not a time it cannot read. It tells the planner to read the deliverables first, then the callers, tests and config each criterion names, to write the plan as soon as every criterion has a demonstration and a seam, and to stop exploring by half the deadline, which is the point the order is sized to. It also says to return the best complete plan with unresolved items as `User:` or `Host:` open questions. It is prose: information, not enforcement. `planning_round` (planning.rs:129) sets `deadline_s: cfg.planner_timeout_s`, the same `cfg` field it passes to `agent_spec` at planning.rs:162. That becomes `AgentInvocation.timeout = Duration::from_secs(timeout_s)` (crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:469), so the figure shown is the figure enforced. The doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry say what finding 2 asked: the two named jobs ran under 600 s, commit 740a9e4 (HISTORY.txt:90) raised the live `planner_timeout_s` to 86400 (athena.toml:224), and this change covers any configured deadline (run tests and other repositories use 600). No refusal rule, prompt file, config, record shape or resume machinery changes. Two tests pin it: a unit test on the brief text for two deadlines and both rounds, and a run test through `Athena::go` that shows the brief figure equals the enforced timeout and that a planner stopped at the deadline still ends the job as a planning stop.

decisions.choice: New field `PlannerInputs.deadline_s: u64`, filled from `JobPlanConfig.planner_timeout_s`. It mirrors the enforced limit and does not reuse a config key for another meaning.
decisions.reason: The config field (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:229, `pub planner_timeout_s: u64`, no doc comment) has its meaning read from its use. `planning_round` passes it to `agent_spec` as `timeout_s` (planning.rs:162). `agent_spec` stores it as `AgentInvocation.timeout: Duration` (crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:406 and 469; crates/athena-agent/src/lib.rs:76). A pass beyond it records 'deadline of {secs}s reached' (crates/athena-agent/src/procs.rs:19-21). So it is the wall-clock limit of one planner call, which is what the planner must size its work to. Config validation refuses zero (config.rs:812-813), so the figure is at least 1. Live value: athena.toml:224 `planner_timeout_s = 86400` (the planner role is the only role this field affects; the critic has its own `critic_timeout_s`, athena.toml:225). The run tests set 600 (run/tests.rs:297). The brief prints whatever config holds.

rejected.option: Persist a draft plan and resume or retry after a planner timeout
rejected.why: Out of scope in the accepted reading: it needs streamed agent output, and the brief is the smaller fix. A timed-out call still ends as a planning stop (planning.rs:190-198).

rejected.option: A refusal or sizing gate in admission
rejected.why: Giving the planner the deadline can prevent the failure, so a refusal rule is not allowed. None is added, so no refused-share figure applies (0 of past readings refused).

decisions.choice: Render the rule in its own `## Deadline` section before `## Report`, not inside the Report text.
decisions.reason: The Report size pin (briefs.rs:3963-4004, `PLANNER_REPORT_BASE_BYTES` = 1749) bounds the Report to the base plus the three named rules. Tests split on `## Report` and take `nth(1)` (briefs.rs:1768, 1803, 1820, 1846, 3971, 4010). A separate section leaves those pins unchanged. The rule constant has no newline and does not contain the text `## Report`, as CODE_CLAIMS_RULE is pinned (briefs.rs:1837-1838). The section is built after the revision block (planner.rs:133-155), so a revision brief carries it too. The History-file test cuts at the next `\n## ` (briefs.rs:3006) and the system-facts test checks only the order of `## System facts` and `## Checks` (briefs.rs:3040-3041); neither sees the new section.

rejected.option: Append to the Report and raise PLANNER_REPORT_BASE_BYTES
rejected.why: It edits an existing pin for no gain, and it puts the figure after the long rules.

rejected.option: Put the section near the top, after the title
rejected.why: Not needed. The section sits in every brief shape, including a revision, and the test checks that it appears once.

decisions.choice: Finding 1 (major, no clock): the rule says the planner has no clock and gives it a measure it can check, a reading order counted in tool calls, with the half-deadline figure kept as the target the order is sized to. Order: (1) the deliverables, (2) the callers, tests and config each criterion names, (3) anything else only once every criterion has a demonstration and a seam. The planner starts writing the plan as soon as the second step is done and every criterion has a demonstration and a seam.
decisions.reason: `planning_grant()` gives the planner Read, Grep and Glob and an empty `commands` map (planning.rs:656-663; pinned by `the_planner_and_critic_grant_has_no_bash_no_git_and_no_writes`, planning.rs:669-674), so it cannot read the time. The producer precedent answers this directly: 'You have no clock of your own. If the commands Bash may run include `date`, note the time ...; without it, count steps against the order above' (briefs.rs:773-774). The planner has no Bash at all, so only the second half applies. The brief therefore says so and does not ask for an action on a time the planner cannot measure. The half-deadline figure stays: it tells the planner the proportion of the deadline that exploration may use, and the order is how it keeps to it. Half is a judgement and an estimate, not measured.

rejected.option: Keep 'stop exploring by N seconds' with no mention of the clock
rejected.why: The planner cannot act on a time it cannot read; this was finding 1.

rejected.option: Give a tool-call count as the limit (for example 40 calls)
rejected.why: No record of tool-call counts or durations per planner run is in the snapshot (records/ is absent), so any such number would be invented. The order of work is checkable without a number.

decisions.choice: The rule's figures are computed and its text is one line: `stop_s = (deadline_s / 2).max(1)`, a template with `{deadline_s}` and `{stop_s}` placeholders filled by a private `fn deadline_section(deadline_s: u64) -> String` that uses `str::replace`.
decisions.reason: A concrete figure is checkable (600 gives 300, 1200 gives 600) and scales with the configured deadline, as the producer's `time_budget_section` takes its figure from the caller and never from a constant (briefs.rs:758-763). The constant stays a plain `&str` the test can check for no newline, like the other rules.

rejected.option: Say only 'well before the deadline' with no figure
rejected.why: The criterion asks for a fraction of the deadline, and a figure is testable.
A `format!` template cannot be a shared `const &str` that the test reads.

decisions.choice: Finding 3 (minor, needle capitalisation): one exact lowercase phrase, `stop exploring by {stop_s} seconds`, is used in the constant and, filled, in the test needles (`stop exploring by 300 seconds`, `stop exploring by 600 seconds`). The deadline phrase is `deadline of {deadline_s} seconds`. The other needles are `sends no plan`, `You have no clock of your own`, `User:` and `Host:`.
decisions.reason: A needle that differs in case from the rule text fails the new test. The rule sentence is written so each needle is a literal substring: '... has a deadline of {deadline_s} seconds ... A planner stopped at the deadline sends no plan ... You have no clock of your own ... Size the reading to stop exploring by {stop_s} seconds (half the deadline) ...'.

rejected.option: Capitalised `Stop exploring by` in the test and lowercase in the rule
rejected.why: They would not match; the test would fail on its own text.

decisions.choice: Finding 2 (minor, the live 600 s trigger is already gone): the DEADLINE_RULE doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry both say that the two failures (jobs 20261114-041123-hvyh and 20261030-113229-kgrg) ran under a 600 s planner limit, that commit 740a9e4 (2026-11-14, 'Raise stage time limits to 24 hours in athena.toml', HISTORY.txt:90) raised the live `planner_timeout_s` to 86400 (athena.toml:224; the CHANGELOG.md:15 'Changed' entry records the same raise), and that this change covers any configured deadline: the run tests set 600 (run/tests.rs:297), and a later lowering or another repository can set a short one.
decisions.reason: A reader of the changelog must not take this change as the fix that ended the two failures in this repository; the raise already did. This change addresses the shared cause that remains: the deadline was never stated to the planner, so any configured deadline can kill it with no plan. It is the same limit the producer entry states (CHANGELOG.md:34: 'the live limit is 86400 s ... the number matters most if the limit is lowered again').

rejected.why: The changelog would overstate the change; this was finding 2.

decisions.choice: Finding 4 (nit): demonstration 5 is written in two labelled parts. The new-behavior part is the brief figure (`deadline of {n} seconds`) and the equality of that figure with the recorded `spec.timeout`, for two configured values (600 and 4321). The regression-guard part is that a planner turn ending in `TimedOut` still ends the job as a planning stop with the unchanged prefix and reason.
decisions.reason: The wrapper sets `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut` and the detail text itself, so the reason text comes from the double; the path that matters (planning.rs:190-198 through `stop_planning`, planning.rs:8-14) is production code that `run_pin_tests.rs:799-841` already pins for the verifier and that this test only guards. A second configured value (4321, as the producer test uses at run/tests.rs:1101) keeps the test from passing on a constant 600.

rejected.option: Present the stop half as new evidence
rejected.why: It checks existing stop handling and is a guard only.

decisions.choice: The test seam for criterion 7 is the existing planner-brief unit tests and planning run tests plus the three check commands, run over the final tree.
decisions.reason: Criterion 7 is a behavior criterion. Its demonstration must name an entry point, a fixture and whether the seam exists. The entry points are `planner_brief(&PlannerInputs)` (planner.rs:95) through the existing tests at briefs.rs:1767, 1802, 1819, 1845, 2817, 2853, 2880, 2999, 3027, 3970 and 4009, and `Athena::go` through `planning_round` through the existing planning run tests that use `run_planned` (run/tests.rs:1356). The fixtures are the `planner_inputs(revision)` helper (briefs.rs:2776-2813) and `repo_with_planning`, `planning_script` and `athena_with` (run/tests.rs:294, 1322, 192). All exist today. The only change to them is one new field in the helper literal (plan step 5).

rejected.option: Leave criterion 7 as a command with no seam
rejected.why: A behavior criterion needs a named seam.

steps: In crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs, add `pub deadline_s: u64` to `PlannerInputs` with a doc comment: the wall-clock limit of one planner call in seconds, as enforced by `agent_spec` (crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:469).

Add `pub(super) const DEADLINE_RULE: &str`, a single-line template with `{deadline_s}` and `{stop_s}`. Its doc comment names the root cause (the planner's fixed deadline was never stated to it, so it explored until killed and left no plan; jobs 20261114-041123-hvyh and 20261030-113229-kgrg, both under a 600 s limit), says that 740a9e4 raised the live value to 86400 and that the rule covers any configured deadline, says it is information and not a refusal, says the planner has Read, Grep and Glob only (`planning_grant`, planning.rs:656-663) so the rule gives an order to count against and not a time, says the half-deadline figure is a judgement and an estimate, and says a test in briefs.rs pins it. The text, with these exact phrases: `This planning call has a deadline of {deadline_s} seconds of wall-clock time. A planner stopped at the deadline sends no plan, and planning for the job stops with nothing kept. You have no clock of your own: your tools are Read, Grep and Glob, which show no time, so count your tool calls against the order below. Sort your reading by what the acceptance criteria need: read the deliverables first, then the callers, tests and config each criterion names, and read anything else only once every criterion has a demonstration and a seam. Size the reading to stop exploring by {stop_s} seconds (half the deadline): once every criterion has a demonstration and a seam, write the plan, even if you have not read everything. Return the best complete plan you have, with anything unresolved as an open question beginning `User:` or `Host:`, instead of reading on.` It has no newline and no `## Report`.

Add a private `fn deadline_section(deadline_s: u64) -> String` that returns `## Deadline`, a blank line and the rule with its two placeholders replaced by `str::replace`, with `stop_s = (deadline_s / 2).max(1)`. In `planner_brief`, after the revision block (planner.rs:155) and before the `## Report` writeln (planner.rs:156), write `\n{section}\n`. Leave the Report text and its constants unchanged.
In crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs, add `deadline_s: cfg.planner_timeout_s` to the `PlannerInputs` literal at planning.rs:129.

In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, add `deadline_s: 600` to the `planner_inputs` helper literal (briefs.rs:2788), then add `planner_brief_states_its_deadline_and_the_stop_early_rule_in_both_rounds` as in demonstration 4, after `planner_brief_requires_code_claims_to_cite_the_code_in_both_rounds` (briefs.rs:1835). Its needles are the exact lowercase phrase `stop exploring by {n/2} seconds`, `deadline of {n} seconds`, `sends no plan`, `You have no clock of your own`, `User:` and `Host:`, all checked on the Deadline section slice.

In crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs, add `the_planner_brief_states_the_enforced_deadline_and_a_planner_deadline_still_stops_planning` as in demonstration 5, near `run_planned` and `prompts_of` (run/tests.rs:1356-1432). Its doc comment says the brief and timeout assertions are the new behavior and the stop assertions are a regression guard.

Add the CHANGELOG.md entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` (CHANGELOG.md:8, 30), as the first bullet. Name the root cause (the planner's fixed deadline was never stated to it, so it explored until killed and left no plan; jobs 20261114-041123-hvyh and 20261030-113229-kgrg), that both ran under 600 s and that 740a9e4 raised the live value to 86400 (athena.toml:224, the Changed entry at CHANGELOG.md:15) so this change covers any configured deadline, the fix (`PlannerInputs.deadline_s`, `DEADLINE_RULE`, the `## Deadline` section, the no-clock sentence and the reading order), that it is information only with no refusal rule (0% of past readings refused) and no draft persistence, resume or retry, that the brief shows whatever config says, that whether planners follow the rule is not measured and that half the deadline is an estimate, and the two test names. Do not touch any prompt file, athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, docs/decisions.md or records/.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p athena-context`, `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix any failure in the files listed.

risks.risk: The live planner deadline is 86400 s, so the rule matters less in this repository today than when the two jobs failed under 600 s, and with 86400 the half-deadline figure is 43200 s, which is harmless but weak.
risks.mitigation: The brief prints whatever `planner_timeout_s` holds, so it stays correct. The 600 s in the accepted reading is the test repository value (run/tests.rs:297) and the value the two jobs ran under; the live athena.toml:224 is 86400 since 740a9e4. The doc comment and the CHANGELOG say so (finding 2). The rule's value is in its fixed 'a planner stopped at the deadline sends no plan' text, in the reading order that does not depend on the figure, and in any shorter configured deadline.

risks.risk: A prose rule does not force the planner to finish in time, so a planner can still hit the deadline. The planner has no clock, so it can only follow the reading order and the call count it keeps itself.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment marks the rule prose-only. The tests pin the brief text, not planner behavior. The changelog says that whether planners follow it is not measured. The half-deadline figure is an estimate and a judgement call. Resume or draft persistence stays a separate request.

risks.risk: A new section could disturb tests that split the brief on `## Report` or pin its size.
risks.mitigation: The section sits before `## Report` and the rule has no `## Report` text, so every split on `## Report` and the size pin (briefs.rs:3988) are unchanged. Step 8 runs the whole of `cargo test -p athena-context` to check this.

risks.risk: The shown figure could drift from the enforced one.
risks.mitigation: The run test asserts both the brief figure and `spec.timeout` from the same run, for 600 and 4321, so a constant fails. Both come from `cfg.planner_timeout_s`, read once at planning.rs:98-101.

risks.risk: The two-deadline unit test could pass by accident because 1200 / 2 = 600, or because other parts of the brief (system facts, history, the quoted plan) contain the phrase.
risks.mitigation: All figure assertions run on the `## Deadline` section slice only, and each brief is also checked for the other value's deadline phrase (`deadline of 1200 seconds` or `deadline of 600 seconds`) and stop phrase, never a bare figure.

risks.risk: A second configured planner timeout of 4321 in the run test might meet a config validation rule not seen in this read.
risks.mitigation: The producer test already runs with a changed limit of 4321 (run/tests.rs:1101); config.rs:812-813 refuses only zero for the planner. Step 8 runs the test; if validation rejects it, the producer picks another positive value.

demonstrations.method: New unit test `planner_brief_states_its_deadline_and_the_stop_early_rule_in_both_rounds` in briefs.rs, next to the planner-brief tests (after briefs.rs:1859). For deadline 600 and 1200, and for `planner_inputs(None)` and `planner_inputs(Some(PlanRevision{ previous: plan(1), findings: vec![finding(Severity::Major, FindingSource::Critic, "F")], resumed_from: None }))`, set `inputs.deadline_s` and build the brief. Assert `brief.matches("## Deadline").count() == 1` and that the heading comes before `## Report`. Slice the section: the text after `## Deadline` up to `## Report`; every further assertion is on that slice, so the system facts, the history or the quoted plan cannot satisfy it. In the slice assert: `deadline of {n} seconds`; `stop exploring by {n/2} seconds` (300 for 600, 600 for 1200); `sends no plan`; `You have no clock of your own`; `User:`; `Host:`. It must NOT contain the other value's deadline phrase (`deadline of 1200 seconds` in the 600 brief and the reverse) nor the other value's stop phrase (`stop exploring by 600 seconds` in the 600 brief, `stop exploring by 300 seconds` in the 1200 brief). The rule text is absent from the part after `## Report`. Also assert `!DEADLINE_RULE.contains('\n')`, `!DEADLINE_RULE.contains("## Report")` and that the constant holds the `{deadline_s}` and `{stop_s}` placeholders.
demonstrations.observes: Each of the four briefs carries its own deadline figure, its own stop figure, the no-clock sentence and the stop-early instruction in its Deadline section, and no brief carries the other deadline.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree the test does not compile, because `deadline_s` and `DEADLINE_RULE` do not exist. With the field but no rule text, every section assertion fails because no `## Deadline` section exists. If the figure were hard-coded to 600, the 1200 briefs would fail. If the stop figure were not computed, the 1200 briefs would fail on `stop exploring by 600 seconds`. If the no-clock sentence were dropped (finding 1), every brief would fail on `You have no clock of your own`. If the rule were left out of a revision brief, the revision cases would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `athena_context::briefs::planner_brief(&PlannerInputs)` (planner.rs:95), reached from the tests module of briefs.rs, where `DEADLINE_RULE` is visible as `super::planner::DEADLINE_RULE` (`pub(super)`, the pattern of CODE_CLAIMS_RULE at briefs.rs:1836). Fixture: the existing `planner_inputs(revision)` helper (briefs.rs:2776-2813), `plan(1)` (briefs.rs:2704) and `finding(...)` (briefs.rs:2766), injected by setting `inputs.deadline_s` on the returned struct. Exists today; plan step 5 adds the `deadline_s` field to the helper literal. No double: the brief builder is production code.

demonstrations.method: New test `the_planner_brief_states_the_enforced_deadline_and_a_planner_deadline_still_stops_planning` in run/tests.rs, near the planning tests (after `run_planned`, run/tests.rs:1356-1373, and `prompts_of`, 1426). For each n in [600, 4321]: build the repository with the config text of `repo_with_planning(1)` (run/tests.rs:294-299) with `planner_timeout_s = n` through `repo_with_config` (run/tests.rs:302); keep an `Arc<Mutex<Vec<Duration>>>` for planner timeouts and a `Calls` log (run/tests.rs:1318); take `planning_script(vec![good_plan()], vec![], calls.clone())` (run/tests.rs:1322) as the inner script and wrap it in an outer `athena_agent::fake::Script`. For `Role::Planner` the wrapper pushes `spec.timeout`, calls the inner script, then sets `turn.outcome = InvocationOutcome::TimedOut`, `turn.structured = None` and `turn.detail = Some(format!("deadline of {n}s reached"))`, as `timing_out` does for the producer (run/tests.rs:7208-7219). Run it with `athena_with(&repo, &state, PASSES, crate::test_support::plenty_of_space, script)` and `finished_job(&athena)` (run/tests.rs:2439). NEW-BEHAVIOR assertions: the first planner prompt (`prompts_of(&calls, Role::Planner)`) contains `deadline of {n} seconds` and `stop exploring by {n/2} seconds`; the recorded planner timeout equals `Duration::from_secs(n)`. REGRESSION-GUARD assertions (existing behavior, the reason text comes from the double): the finished job's state is `OutcomeState::Failed`; the reason starts with `athena_data::records::PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX` and contains `the planner did not complete: deadline of {n}s reached`; no `Role::Producer` call is in `calls`.
demonstrations.observes: For two configured values the brief the fake agent received carries that value, the enforced timeout is that many seconds, and a planner stop at the deadline still ends the job as a planning stop with the unchanged reason.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree the planner prompt has no `deadline of 600 seconds`, so the first assertion fails. If planning.rs filled the field from any value other than `cfg.planner_timeout_s` (for example a constant 600), the 4321 case would show a brief figure that differs from the `spec.timeout` of 4321 s. If the change altered the timeout path (planning.rs:190-198), the guard assertions on the reason or state would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` into `planning_round` (planning.rs:129-198), with `stop_planning` (planning.rs:8-14) and `failure` producing the Failed state. Fixture: a fake agent script (`athena_agent::fake::Script`) injected through `athena_with(...)` (run/tests.rs:192), as in `run_planned` (run/tests.rs:1356-1373) and `timing_out` (7208-7219). The wrapper only records `spec.timeout` and rewrites the planner's turn outcome and detail. Brief building, the `agent_spec` timeout and the stop path stay production code. Exists today: all helpers are read at the cited lines. No plan step adds a helper; step 6 adds only the test function.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG.md hunk and the diff stat. The new bullet goes under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` (CHANGELOG.md:8 and 30), above the entry at line 32. It names the root cause (the planner's fixed deadline was never stated to it; jobs 20261114-041123-hvyh and 20261030-113229-kgrg), that both ran under 600 s, that 740a9e4 raised the live value to 86400 and this covers any configured deadline, the fix (`deadline_s`, `DEADLINE_RULE`, the `## Deadline` section with the no-clock sentence), that it is information only with no refusal rule (0% of past readings refused) and no resume or draft persistence, and the test names. The stat lists only the five deliverables.
demonstrations.observes: Only the five deliverable files appear. No prompt file, athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, docs/decisions.md or records/ path is in the stat, and the changelog hunk (`git diff -- CHANGELOG.md`) names the root cause and 740a9e4.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs, on the final tree. Existing planner-brief tests and planning run tests are the regression guard for the shared paths this change touches. They pass only if (a) the `planner_inputs` helper literal carries `deadline_s` (the only test construction site of `PlannerInputs`; the other is planning.rs:129), (b) the new `## Deadline` section leaves the Report text and its size pin intact (briefs.rs:3963-4004) and does not disturb the `split("## Report").nth(1)` tests, (c) the prompt-set budgets are unchanged (`system_facts_budgets_match_computed`, crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs), (d) the planning round-trip tests in run/tests.rs that use `run_planned` still run with the field filled from `cfg`, and (e) the refusal-corpus tests that `include_str!` CHANGELOG.md (crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs:1138, 1217, 1250, 1749, 2986, 3033, 3073, 3128, 3187) still find their needles, since an added entry removes none. The recorded Athena checks on the final tree count as evidence (D115).
demonstrations.observes: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` exit 0, so every existing planner-brief and planning run test passes with the new field set.
demonstrations.fails_without: A `PlannerInputs` literal missing `deadline_s` fails to compile (E0063), so `cargo test` and clippy fail. Text added inside the Report, or a rule constant that contains `## Report` or a newline, fails the pins at briefs.rs:1837-1838 or 3988. An unformatted new line fails `cargo fmt --check`. An unused or needlessly cloned helper in planner.rs fails `clippy -D warnings`. A prompt-file edit would fail `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`.
